summary: Wasco County, OR site on Mount Hood NF: a 1934 tree crow's nest with tent and phone, later abandoned; no source describes what remains today.

facts.status_note: Both listings say the 1934 setup was abandoned; neither says what, if anything, remains

events.note: Crow's nest erected in a tree with tent and phone (firetower.org); listed as crow's nest and camp (firelookout.com)

evidence.supports: 1934 tree crow's nest with tent and phone, since abandoned
evidence.quote: In 1934 a tree crow's net and tent with phone was erected on this site and has since been abandoned.

evidence.supports: 1934 crow's nest and camp, abandoned; the listing mentions no tent or telephone
about 17 miles southeast of Mount Hood
listed under Mount Hood National Forest, Wasco County
administered by the U.S. Forest Service
separate Montana Boulder Point Lookout; NRHP nomination calls it an example of the 1931 L-4 lookout house design
evidence.quote: Boulder Point Lookout is an excellent example of the 1931-patten L-4 Lookout House

evidence.supports: the Montana lookout is in Ravalli County, Montana

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firetower.org describes a crow's nest in a tree with a tent and phone; firelookout.com describes only a crow's nest and camp, with no tent or phone. The story gives both and says the second is briefer, without choosing one. Neither page mentions a tower or building, so the story does not claim a disagreement about structure type. The brief's kind 'platform' is supported by neither page.

sources.title: Boulder Point Lookout (Montana), National Register of Historic Places nomination

notes_for_editor: Thin record: two one-line listings and a roster entry. No photos, staffing or later history found. The brief's 'platform' kind is not supported. Search results mix in the Montana Boulder Point Lookout (a different, NRHP-listed structure); it is used only for a disambiguation sentence in the story, not for facts. Two searches run.
